trust_decision.summary: Whether a publish reader may fetch a file under the workspace data tree is decided per gin route handler in kernel/server/serve.go from the role in the gin context (every publish token, including the anonymous account, carries RoleReader), and after the fix also by joining the requested widget/emoji package name against references found in documents that reader is allowed to see; at the pinned commit only /assets/ consults publishAccess at all, the four data-directory mounts are gated by model.CheckAuth alone.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names templates, snippets and export artifacts, so an engineer lands on serveTemplates / serveSnippets / serveExport; all six vulnerable data-directory mounts are registered in one 20-line block (serve.go:323-481) that passes only model.CheckAuth, which authenticates but never authorises a publish reader.

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /snippets/*filepath (model.CheckSnippetAccessableInPublish, called from the handler's read-only branch)
shared helper behind the widget and emoji entry points: getPublishResourceRefs / widgetPackagesInTree / walkPublishResourceHTML / publishResourceURLPath / normalizePublishResourcePath
fix_sites.module_kind: model / document reference extraction and URL normalisation
server / static route registration (group gains model.CheckAdminRole)

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /snippets/*filepath (path clean + 404/403 split for read-only roles)
shared lower-level primitive registerStaticFileHandlers / cleanStaticRelativePath / serveStaticFile, mounted by the widgets, plugins, emojis, templates and snippets routes

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The publish-access question is answered by a brand-new model-layer reference resolver ('which resources do the documents this reader may see reference'), while an equally plausible fix lives in the older file-level check CheckAbsPathAccessableByPublishAccess (kernel/model/publish_access.go:300-335) that /assets/ and /api/file/getFile already use, so the new module can be dismissed as a helper the handlers already call; the same argument covers the untouched /public/ mount, which is documented as an intentional direct-access folder (kernel/util/working.go:542).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A published (visible, password-free) document that embeds a widget, an enabled plugin or a custom emoji must keep serving those files to anonymous readers, and snippets not marked disabledInPublish must keep loading in publish mode; a blanket 'read-only roles get 403 on /widgets/, /plugins/, /emojis/, /snippets/' fix breaks published rendering. Local desktop requests must also keep reaching /export/ and /templates/, which today works only because CheckAuth promotes localhost to RoleAdministrator.

O6_input_shapes: request path traversal and absolute/volume segments: /../secret, ../secret, /package/../../secret (cleanStaticRelativePath)
directory request with and without trailing slash (/widgets/example/ resolves to index.html; /widgets/example/index.html is treated as a distinct relative path)
symlinked package directory allowed at the first segment while a symlink nested inside the package that escapes it is rejected (EvalSymlinks + IsSubPath)
resource reference written as an absolute local URL with query string: http://127.0.0.1:6806/emojis/icon.png?v=1
resource reference with traversal into another mount: /widgets/../templates/private.md must authorise nothing
resource reference with a non-local host: https://example.com/widgets/external/ must not authorise a local package of the same name
carrier node types in the stored document: widget, iframe, HTML block and inline HTML tokens
snippet URL shapes: name plus extension (allow.css / disabled.js) vs an on-disk file that is absent from conf.json (conflicting found/accessable booleans)
role shapes: RoleReader/RoleVisitor (publish token) vs RoleAdministrator (localhost or lock-screen session)

O7_producer.where: kernel/bazaar/plugin.go:28-63 and kernel/bazaar/package.go:114-131 (plugin.json / widget.json disabledInPublish), kernel/model/snippet.go:62-85 (data/snippets/conf.json), kernel/model/publish_access.go:60-94 (data/.siyuan/publishAccess.json, 30s in-process cache)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET|HEAD /public/*filepath - gin static mount of data/public registered with no middleware at all, so any client (publish reader, LAN visitor) reads it with no publish-access or admin decision
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The mount is documented as an intentional direct-access folder for sharing links (comment at kernel/util/working.go:542, issue 8593) and holds no notebook or document, so no publishAccess item can describe it and the advisory's 'publish access controls' property does not reach it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package and file as the landing point, 5 lines below serveTemplates

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a seventh data-directory mount (e.g. /storage/ or /plugins-index/) registered with gin Static and model.CheckAuth only
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file registers six mounts one per data subdirectory in a single block, so a maintainer adding a new exportable data folder would copy the neighbouring line verbatim and inherit the same missing check

O8b_injection_room.sibling: authorisation from a different reference carrier than widget/iframe/HTML-block tokens - a Markdown image or link pointing at /widgets/<name>/ or /emojis/<icon>, or a document IAL attribute
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: emojisInTree itself already reads the document icon from IAL (kernel/model/assets.go:2009-2014) and asset links are collected through getAssetsLinkDestsWithAttributeViewItemFilter from docAssets (kernel/model/assets.go:543-558), so a maintainer copying either helper would cover a carrier the fix does not

O8b_injection_room.sibling: extending CheckAbsPathAccessableByPublishAccess with a data/widgets and data/emojis branch instead of adding a new model file
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: that function is the one place /assets/ and /api/file/getFile already route through, so a maintainer fixing the same report would naturally add the branch there rather than duplicate the logic in a new file

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a single path allowlist enforced in the publish reverse proxy instead of in each handler
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the publish port is the one choke point every anonymous request crosses (rewrite sets only the target URL today, RoundTrip sets only the auth token), so enforcing the resource policy there is a plausible alternative design

O9_family: CWE-862 missing authorization / broken access control (A01) on static-file routes: publish-access and admin-only gating absent from the data-directory HTTP mounts (templates, snippets, export artifacts, widgets, plugins, emojis)

O10_build.language: Go (kernel) with a pnpm/Electron frontend that is not needed for the affected code
O10_build.toolchain: Go 1.26 module rooted at kernel/go.mod; CGO_ENABLED=1 and -tags "fts5 sqlcipher" (scripts/linux-build.sh:64-69,104-110), so a C toolchain plus the sqlcipher sqlite source is required
O10_build.project_tests: Go tests in kernel/model and kernel/server: existing publish-access coverage in kernel/model/publish_access_test.go, plus kernel/server/serve_assets_test.go and kernel/server/serve_svg_test.go for the static handlers; the fix adds kernel/model/publish_resource_access_test.go and kernel/server/serve_static_test.go, neither of which exists at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Put model.CheckAdminRole on the /widgets/, /plugins/ and /emojis/ groups by analogy with the templates fix (or gate each mount on 'some document references this package' without checking that document's publish access), then verify with one reader request for a publish-disabled widget.

out_of_scope_notes: kernel/server/serve.go:538-599 serves /appearance/*filepath from the appearance tree and kernel/model/session.go:289-295 exempts that prefix from CheckAuth; it serves application assets, not workspace data, so it is outside this advisory's protection and was not pursued.

The same commit also replaces gin's Static with registerStaticFileHandlers/serveStaticFile (fix.diff:503-594), adding symlink resolution, index.html handling and IsSensitivePath checks; that is traversal/symlink hardening adjacent to, but not part of, the publish-access advisory, and it is counted once as a shared fix site rather than as separate entry points.
kernel/model/export.go:1224 rewrites "/emojis" to "emojis" in exported documents; noted only as evidence that published/exported pages legitimately reference the emoji mount, not pursued further.
unverified: Repo size in MB: no shell was available in this session, so the 5 MB / 1.5 GB thresholds were not measured; the tree is clearly not tiny (2616+ files) and there is no vendored node_modules or binary blob set visible, so it is unlikely to be giant.
